hints: Start by counting carbons, use the volume of carbon dioxide to work out how many moles of carbon came from each mole of X.
Remember that a positive 2,4-DNPH test means X must contain a C=O group, so it is an aldehyde or a ketone.
Combine the 3-carbon count with the negative iodoform test, which rules out any molecule containing the CH3CO group.
walkthrough:
**Find the number of carbon atoms from combustion**

All the carbon in X ends up as $\text{CO}_2$. First convert the gas volume to moles.

$$n(\text{CO}_2) = \frac{14.4}{24.0} = 0.60 \text{ mol}$$

**Calculate carbons per molecule of X**

0.20 mol of X gave 0.60 mol of $\text{CO}_2$.

$$\text{C atoms per X} = \frac{0.60}{0.20} = 3$$
So X contains 3 carbon atoms. This immediately rules out any 6-carbon compound.

**Use the 2,4-DNPH test**

A positive result with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine reagent, giving an orange crystalline precipitate, is the classic test for a carbonyl compound.

$$\text{X is an aldehyde or ketone: RCHO or RCOR'}$$
This rules out alcohols like propan-1-ol, which do not react.

**Use the negative iodoform test**

No yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ means a negative triiodomethane (iodoform) test. A positive test needs a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group, found in methyl ketones and ethanal.

$$\text{positive: } \text{CH}_3\text{CO-R} \text{, negative: no } \text{CH}_3\text{CO} \text{ group}$$
Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, would be positive, but propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group and is negative. That fits all three clues.

options.A: Hexan-3-one, CH3CH2COCH2CH2CH3, is a ketone so it gives a positive 2,4-DNPH test and a negative iodoform test, but it has 6 carbons. 0.20 mol would give 1.20 mol CO2, which is 28.8 dm3, not 14.4 dm3.
options.B: Propanal, CH3CH2CHO, has 3 carbons, matching the combustion data. As an aldehyde it gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. As it has no CH3CO group it gives a negative iodoform test. All three properties match.
options.C: Propan-1-ol, CH3CH2CH2OH, has 3 carbons so fits the combustion data, but alcohols do not react with 2,4-DNPH reagent. This is the trap of only checking the carbon count.
options.D: Propanone, CH3COCH3, has 3 carbons and gives a positive 2,4-DNPH test, but it contains a CH3CO group so it gives a positive iodoform test with yellow CHI3 precipitate. The question states X does not give this precipitate.
